THE BEDROOM: THE FIRST LOOK

A design pass for Wyatt and Al. November 10, 2026. Card 3175.

Nothing here is in the game. Every picture is the real game (v31.11) on a phone, with the new paint laid in by a test rig.

1 · What a new player sees today

A new player wins the opening battle, taps CONTINUE, and stands in the bedroom for the first time. Sarge's window covers the lower half, so the first thing seen is the wall.

Why it feels dry, measured

29 %of the screen is the rug: one flat blue shape with one line round it.
8 apartThe wall and the floor are almost one tan (under 10 reads as one colour). 41 % of the room is that one beige.
No sunThe window shows a sunny day and no light comes into the room.

2 · Three moves

Each one can be taken alone. Together they are the proposal.

MOVE 1 · A fuzzy rug, on by default

Wyatt's alternative. Nobody picks it: it is simply the floor of every bedroom with no other rug out. It is drawn fresh in the style guide's look: a cloud edge, three flat tones, little fur ticks.

The same rug in eight colours. Under each: the figure that is hardest to see on it, and how clearly it stands out (under 10 is weak, over 15 is clear).

4 · It holds everywhere

Every rug the game sells, on the new boards under the new sun. A player who owns a rug keeps it: only the floor round it and the light on it change.

Safari's engine paints it the same as Chrome (0 page errors in both). The whole proposal adds about 78 KB of drawing to one paint of the room (14 to 34 thousandths of a second in Chrome, 50 to 81 in Safari's engine), once per paint, never per frame.

For Al

Wyatt asked that you look at this before anything is built. Nothing is final.

  • The fuzzy rug, the boards, the wall's colour and the light are a session's drawings in the style guide's look. They are yours to redraw, change or throw out.
  • The bare wall left of the shelf (it shows on wide phones) is left empty on purpose. It is a place for something of yours, if you want it.
  • The characters in the room (the army men, the bear, the piggy) are untouched.
  • To answer: say it in your own words, or draw over any picture and send it back.

5 · Questions for Wyatt

1 · The rug's colour

  • Blue (the pick of this pass): everyone stays easy to see and the sun shows on it.
  • Ivory, the white one: your first thought; the white flags fade on it.
  • Another colour from the sheet.

2 · Which moves

  • All three (the pick).
  • The rug alone: the smallest build.
  • The rug and the sun.

3 · Who gets the fuzzy rug

  • Every bedroom with no other rug out, old players too (the pick): it is the floor, nobody picks.
  • New players only.

4 · The old flat blue rug

  • Retire it (the pick). One switch on a device brings the old room back.
  • Keep it as a free rug in the RUGS tab.

5 · The other fuzzy colours

  • Leave them out for now (the pick).
  • Sell some in the RUGS tab at 250 stars, like Dylan's five. He left the shags out on October 14.

6 · The sun on every rug

  • Yes (the pick): the four panes lie on whatever rug is out. That includes Laura's seven finished rugs, so her word is wanted too.
  • Only on the default rug.

7 · Laura

  • Send her the same page (the pick): her style guide pass is what is live on this room today.
  • Al only, as asked.

6 · What a build would touch

THE PIECEWHERE IT IS PAINTED TODAY
The rug (move 1)Four places: the room, the mom raid's floor (two painters), the bedroom's small ticket picture. The smallest build.
The sun (move 2)New: three small drawings (the glow, the four panes, the beam), day and night, in the room only.
The boards and the wall (move 3)The widest build. The same two colours are also painted in the mom raid, the strip that runs the floor to the bottom of a tablet, the magnifying glass, the wallpaper and curtain cards, and Fort Green's small bedroom. Bought wallpapers are not touched. The battlefields keep their own boards.
The sheetFour tiles on the character sheet today (the proposed room, the two rugs, the sun). The game's own tiles R 001, R 002, R 003 and R 034 change when it lands.
